purpose.text: InfoDot is the hub and parent of the Dot ecosystem: one sign-in that opens every Dot platform, and the business workspace around it (Knowledge, a directory of live platforms, People, analytics). The experience should help business owners understand their business, access useful collective knowledge, make better decisions and recognise their progress.

evidence.summary: InfoDot is the hub and parent of the Dot ecosystem and the business workspace around its identity provider.

Section 3, "InfoDot": understanding, practical guidance, progress, opportunity and belonging; users understand their business, access collective knowledge, make better decisions and recognise progress.

audience.segment: Business owners and the people who work for them, from small businesses through enterprises
audience.description: Owners and executives, department heads, project managers, information and document managers, IT administrators and employees. They arrive between tasks to find an answer or a document, open the right Dot platform and see who works under the company.

evidence.summary: Lists these roles and this arrival pattern. A declaration by the product owner, not research.

audience.description: The owner directs that small-business owners feel respected and equipped with sophisticated tools regardless of company size. Whether this is the primary segment is not recorded (see unknowns).

evidence.summary: Section 3, "InfoDot": small business owners must feel respected and equipped.

positioning.text: InfoDot is the origin of the ecosystem and has its own identity, "The Yard", drawn from shipping-container ownership: every company has an owner code and everything it owns carries a reference. It is business, not social, and it is not a dark control-room interface, a generic sidebar-and-cards SaaS layout or a social platform.

constraints: Identity concept "The Yard": owner code and reference on everything owned; area colours as container liveries (DESIGN.md).
Standard navigation (top bar, tabs, breadcrumbs); no sidebar (DESIGN.md).
Light and dark themes of equal quality (PRODUCT.md).
Text at or above 4.5:1 in both themes, keyboard navigation, visible focus, reduced motion respected, responsive from 375px (PRODUCT.md).
Each page is laid out for its job, not from one card template (DESIGN.md).
Tokens live in resources/css/infodot.css; this profile cites that file by hash and does not copy tokens.
prohibited: The dark control-room look of Dot.Memory, Dot.Central or Dot.Projects (PRODUCT.md).
Sidebar, gradient text, side-stripe borders, identical card grids, decorative hero blocks, stencil type for paragraphs (DESIGN.md).

forbidden.rule: Do not state or imply a number of customers, businesses, users or documents unless it is read from the application's own live data.
Do not show testimonials, quotes or reviews unless a real, attributable one has been supplied.
Do not claim compliance, certification, audit or security status that has not been established and cited.
Do not advertise roadmap items (such as shared files through a Dot.Files API, or approvals) as available until they are built and verified.

evidence_required: any number about customers or usage
any statement about security, privacy or legal compliance

experience_standards.expression: Design against the six intended feelings in emotional_promise: understanding, practical guidance, progress, opportunity, belonging, respected and equipped.
Small-business owners are treated as professionals with sophisticated tools regardless of size: no "starter" tone, full capability, presentable references and exports.
Identity is "The Yard": ownership references, area liveries and stencilled stamps instead of counters (DESIGN.md).
Honest navigation and server-side visibility (PRODUCT.md). InfoDot is the identity provider other platforms trust.
Progress and understanding are shown in the owner's business terms with their source. No invented proof.
Each page is laid out for its job. The area band and breadcrumbs answer "where am I".
InfoDot is the sign-in hub: hand-offs to other Dot platforms preserve context and use shared names, while InfoDot keeps its own identity.

domain_overrides.reason: DESIGN.md: mustard plates and the Platforms band carry ink, not white, because white on mustard is 2.8:1. The area colour yields to contrast.

overrides.reason: The owner's brief names six specific intended feelings for InfoDot; the ecosystem-level feelings alone are too general to design against.
The owner's brief singles out small-business owners being respected and equipped as a defining InfoDot outcome.
InfoDot is the identity provider every other platform trusts, so honest navigation and server-side visibility carry more weight here than the ecosystem baseline.
InfoDot's product definition sets a plain-language, business-not-social voice that is more specific than the ecosystem default.

unknowns.question: InfoDot's docs/infodot-ui-design-guide.md asks for an interface that "feels like a control center". PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md say InfoDot must not resemble the dark control-room look and define "The Yard". Which document governs is not recorded. This draft records PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md and cites the guide as conflicting; it does not decide. Owner decision needed.
PRODUCT.md lists users from small businesses through enterprises; the owner's brief emphasises small-business owners. Which segment is primary is not recorded.
The brief asks the experience to reinforce belonging; PRODUCT.md forbids social counters and likes and says business, not social. How belonging is expressed without social mechanics is undecided.

No measured customer outcome or feeling data is held for InfoDot. PRODUCT.md states that no customer counts, testimonials or compliance claims exist and none may be invented. Every emotional_promise item is intended, not measured.
What "opportunity" means as something a user can see or do in InfoDot is not defined in PRODUCT.md. No feature is claimed for it.
InfoDot's first meaningful result (BXP-08) is not defined, so no onboarding rule is bound for it.

This profile extends dot-ecosystem because InfoDot is a Dot platform. PRODUCT.md calls InfoDot the hub and parent of the ecosystem with its own identity. Whether the hub should inherit ecosystem rules or define them is the owner's call.
PRODUCT.md describes the legal pages as POPIA-aligned. Under this profile's compliance-claims rule, that wording needs a cited basis before it appears in public copy.
